answer: A fabricated identity can be made to cost time, not money. An account sits out a cooldown before earning, and early submissions are graded more strictly, so each costs wall-clock time capital cannot compress. The registry keeps only a cipher over the applicant record, enough to re-check eligibility. Review seats form a trellis, no panel sharing a majority, so a bought quorum costs far more than one reviewer. A rejected answer burns its bond and requeues the identity. A verified signal, a long attested history, shortens the wait, but cannot be mass-produced. Fraud scales with time, not money.
